title: RWB-S8-E1023-APP: the five read operations and the four consumed operation names of the case record view have no published baseline, and the freshness, scope and mask answers of the owners are unnamed
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2, R7.3 and R9; context pack S8 rwb-deviation; split plan story line RWB-S8-E1023-APP; legacy RWB-E1-023 sections 3, 4 and 12; FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A1.4, A2.2 and Screens; TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 T5.2, T5.3 and T6.2
section: Metadata (Depends on (build), Contract dependencies); Sections 3, 4, 7, 11, 12.1, 12.2, 12.8 and 15
description: (1) No source publishes a read operation for the case record view: the legacy story gives five GET endpoints on /api/recovery/v1, the Ownership Map gives S8 two write operations and no read, and the split plan gives this slice one C row and no H row. (2) The four consumed reads have no published operation names: the rwb-case case-record read, the rwb-source-data account, party and contact read, the rwb-source-data contact-history read and the rwb-document document-list read. (3) The freshness answer of a section becomes a stamp on the owner's answer (dataAsOf and a freshness per product) and no source publishes its shape. (4) The scope filter and the masking rule by role are rwb-access's and no source publishes the read that answers them for the case record page.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-023 sections 3, 4 and 12 (five GET endpoints, AceSourceQuery, FieldMasker, AccessEventPublisher, InteractionLedgerReader); context pack S8 ownership rows (REST operations provided 2, both writes; tables 1; jobs 0); split plan slice RWB-S8-E1023-APP (H empty, C RWB-P3-E1023-CON); TSD S8 T5.2 (calls through published interfaces), T5.3 and T6.2; FSD S8 A1.4 and Screens
area: Contract surface, interface names and freshness
proposed: Publish the five read paths on /api/recovery/deviation/v1 with the shapes of legacy section 12 and the error envelope of RWB-P3-E1023-CON; declare the four consumed operations as placeholders with their owners and fakes; carry dataAsOf and a per-product freshness answer on every data-product answer; declare the authorise, mask and AC-READ accept of rwb-access as one consumed operation; confirm each placeholder with its owner before the tag

title: RWB-S8-E1023-APP: a P3 Case and workflow module story is placed in rwb-deviation with an empty build row, and the plan gives the slice no platform dependency although seven pattern rows add one
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R5.6, R5.7 and R9; split plan story line RWB-S8-E1023-APP; legacy RWB-E1-023 metadata (Module P3 Case and workflow); context pack S8 rwb-deviation; Architecture v5 slide 4
section: Metadata (Service, Wave, Depends on (build), Contract dependencies); Sections 1, 2, 6, 10, 12.1, 13 and 18
description: (1) The legacy story names its module P3 Case and workflow and its service facts are rwb-case's, while the plan places this APP slice in rwb-deviation (S8) with C RWB-P3-E1023-CON and no H row, so two services appear to serve the same read-only page. (2) The pattern set carries DP03, DP06, DP07, DP08, DP14, DP15 and DP19, and the DP table makes each of them an H dependency on a platform contract story (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, E1042, E1043, E1037, E1047, E1044 and N001), yet the plan's build row is empty. (3) The story wave is 1 by W-MAP for EP01 while the service wave is 2 in Arch v5, so the R5.6 rule applies and only the W-MAP wave is kept.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-023 metadata row Module P3 Case and workflow and section 12 endpoints on /api/recovery/v1; split plan slice with H [] and C [RWB-P3-E1023-CON]; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP rows 03, 06, 07, 08, 14, 15 and 19 with dependency added; R5.6 wave map EP01 to 1; context pack S8 wave 2; Architecture v5 slide 4 (P3 Case, S8 Deviation)
proposed: Keep the plan's service, lane, C row and empty H row as they stand; record the slice as the secondary serving of the page with the deviation block and the assembly as its own and the case header consumed from RWB-P3-E1023-CON; declare the seven platform contracts as build prerequisites and fakes without editing the metadata row; keep wave 1 by R5.6 and mark the release tentative

title: RWB-S8-E1023-APP: the plan assigns the slice no legacy acceptance criterion while it keeps thirteen legacy test cases, and the legacy criteria lose their owned ids
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.7, R7.2 s7 and s16, R7.3 and R9; split plan story line RWB-S8-E1023-APP (acs empty, tcs_legacy 13); legacy RWB-E1-023 sections 7 and 16
description: The story line gives acs as an empty list and tcs_legacy as the thirteen legacy cases of RWB-E1-023, so no legacy AC id is owned by this slice, although the legacy story holds twelve criteria and TC-E1-023-01 to TC-E1-023-10, -12 and -13 trace to them one to one and TC-E1-023-11 is an access test with no AC. The template forbids a scenario without an origin tag and forbids inventing business values, so the twelve criteria are restated as new under D-RCV-60 with the legacy scenario values kept word for word, and the thirteen test cases keep their legacy ids and their covers mapping.
evidence: Split plan slice RWB-S8-E1023-APP acs [] and tcs_legacy 13; legacy RWB-E1-023 section 7 (AC1 to AC12) and section 16 (TC-E1-023-01 to -13, TC-11 level Access with no AC); Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s7 origin tag rule and R9 placeholder rule
proposed: Keep acs empty in the fragment and restate AC1 to AC12 as new (D-RCV-60) with the legacy values; carry TC-E1-023-01 to TC-E1-023-13 unchanged and map TC-E1-023-11 to the access refusal; record the mapping in section 18 so the legacy criteria remain traceable to their legacy ids

title: RWB-S8-E1023-APP: the story wave is 1 by the business-epic map while the service wave is 2 in Arch v5, and the section timeout and the six lists have no published values for this page
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.6, R5.7 and R9; context pack S8 rwb-deviation; split plan story line RWB-S8-E1023-APP; legacy RWB-E1-023 section 13; FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A1.4
description: (1) R5.6 gives EP01 wave 1 and the service wave is 2, so the story keeps wave 1 and one conflict is recorded per service and business epic. (2) The legacy solution plan sets caserecord.section.timeout.ms = 3000 as an assumption of the monolith and no source publishes the parameter row, the label set or the six lists of values for this page under DP-06 and DP-07. (3) The release is 30 November 2026 for a service that enters wave 2, which is kept unchanged and tentative per R1 U7.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.6 wave map; context pack S8 wave 2; split plan slice wave 1 and release 30 November 2026; legacy RWB-E1-023 section 13 (parameter caserecord.section.timeout.ms = 3000 assumed, DL11; masking rules, labels, LOV-ACTION-CODE, LOV-CONTACT-RESULT, LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-CONTACT-TYPE, LOV-PARTY-ROLE); FSD S8 A1.4
proposed: Keep wave 1 and the release as they stand and mark the release tentative; read the section timeout and the six lists as parameters and reference data of rwb-case with no value copied into code, and confirm the parameter row with the P3 owner before the tag
